"Crea un juego de ritmo tipo Piano Tiles. Permite importar archivos de música propios y detecta el ritmo para generar las notas automáticamente. Incluye dos tipos de notas: notas cortas que se tocan una sola vez, y notas largas que deben mantenerse presionadas mientras descienden. La velocidad de caída se ajusta según la velocidad de cada canción. Cuatro niveles de dificultad claramente diferenciados: Normal, notas grandes y caída lenta; Hard, notas más pequeñas y caída más rápida; Extreme, caída rápida y muchas notas combinadas; Demon, caída muy rápida y gran densidad de notas simultáneas. El diseño debe ser limpio, sin elementos que se sobrepongan ni errores de capas.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:
  mousemove <x> <y>           move mouse to a given position
  mousedown [button]          press mouse down
  mouseup [button]            press mouse up
  mousewheel <dx> <dy>        scroll mouse wheel

Save as:
  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element
  pdf                         save page as pdf

Tabs:
  tab-list                    list all tabs
  tab-new [url]               create a new tab
  tab-close [index]           close a browser tab
  tab-select <index>          select a browser tab

Storage:
  state-load <filename>       loads browser storage (authentication) state from a file
  state-save [filename]       saves the current storage (authentication) state to a file
  cookie-list                 list all cookies (optionally filtered by domain/path)
  cookie-get <name>           get a specific cookie by name
  cookie-set <name> <value>   set a cookie with optional flags
  cookie-delete <name>        delete a specific cookie
  cookie-clear                clear all cookies
  localstorage-list           list all localstorage key-value pairs
  localstorage-get <key>      get a localstorage item by key
  localstorage-set <key> <value> set a localstorage item
  localstorage-delete <key>   delete a localstorage item
  localstorage-clear          clear all localstorage
  sessionstorage-list         list all sessionstorage key-value pairs
  sessionstorage-get <key>    get a sessionstorage item by key
  sessionstorage-set <key> <value> set a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-delete <key> delete a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-clear        clear all sessionstorage

Network:

export function formatTime(seconds) {
  if (!Number.isFinite(seconds) || seconds < 0) seconds = 0
  const minutes = Math.floor(seconds / 60)
  const rest = Math.floor(seconds % 60)
  return `${minutes}:${String(rest).padStart(2, '0')}`
}

export function clamp(value, min, max) {
  return Math.min(max, Math.max(min, value))
}

export function hashString(value) {
  let hash = 2166136261
  for (let i = 0; i < value.length; i += 1) {
    hash ^= value.charCodeAt(i)
    hash = Math.imul(hash, 16777619)
  }
  return hash >>> 0
}

export function mulberry32(seed) {
  let state = seed >>> 0
  return function random() {
    state += 0x6d2b79f5
    let value = state
    value = Math.imul(value ^ (value >>> 15), value | 1)
    value ^= value + Math.imul(value ^ (value >>> 7), value | 61)
    return ((value ^ (value >>> 14)) >>> 0) / 4294967296
  }
}

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable Piano Tiles-style rhythm game in the empty repo, with local music import + automatic beat detection, tap/hold notes, adaptive fall speed by song tempo, and four clearly distinct difficulties (Normal, Hard, Extreme, Demon).
- Clean visual design with no overlapping UI or layer errors, responsive for desktop/mobile.

## Requirements
- Import user music files and auto-detect rhythm to generate notes.
- Two note types: short taps and long holds (must remain pressed as they descend).
- Fall speed adapts to each song’s speed/BPM.
- Four difficulty levels clearly differentiated:
  - Normal: large notes, slow fall.
  - Hard: smaller notes, faster fall.
  - Extreme: fast fall, many combined notes.
  - Demon: very fast fall, high density of simultaneous notes.
- Clean design without overlaps/layer errors.
- Build now, do not ask clarifying questions; note assumptions when finished.
- Verify with small JPEG screenshots (viewport max 1280px wide); read only latest image.

## Decisions
- Built a dependency-free static site (`index.html`, CSS, ES modules) served from repo root.
- Four-lane gameplay using keys `D F J K` and four touch pads.
- Built-in songs are procedurally composed/synthesized and were pre-rendered to MP3 assets for fast startup; runtime synthesis remains as fallback.
- Imported audio is analyzed fully client-side using Web Audio + FFT spectral flux onset detection and autocorrelation tempo estimation.
- Difficulty settings live in `js/data.js`; chart generation and fall-speed scaling in `js/chart.js`.
- UI is Spanish, dark neon/glass aesthetic with local Sora + Space Mono fonts.
- Imported tracks persist only for the current session; scores/best records use `localStorage`.
- Debug handle exposed as `window.__pulse = { game, state }`.

## Work State

### Completed
- Static app structure, game menu, track library, difficulty cards, launch bar, import modal, pause/results/help overlays.
- Chart generation for built-in and imported audio, including taps, holds, chords, fall-speed scaling.
- Canvas gameplay engine with four lanes, notes, hold bodies, judgment line, counts, combo, accuracy, score, effects, pause/resume, results.
- Beat detector implemented; validated on a synthetic 124 BPM WAV, detected 123 BPM with 98% confidence and 47 onsets.
- Import flow tested end-to-end; imported track was added and played successfully.
- Built-in audio pre-rendered to MP3:
  - `assets/audio/aurora-drive.mp3`

# Pulse Tiles

A dependency-free, four-lane rhythm game that runs entirely in the browser. Pick one of four built-in tracks or import your own audio, choose a difficulty, and tap or hold the tiles as they cross the judgement line.

## Play

No build step or package install is required. Serve the repository root with any static server:

```bash
python3 -m http.server 3002
```

Then open `http://localhost:3002`.

## Controls

| Action | Keyboard | Touch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Lane 1 | `D` | Left pad |
| Lane 2 | `F` | Second pad |
| Lane 3 | `J` | Third pad |
| Lane 4 | `K` | Right pad |
| Pause / resume | `Esc` | Pause button |
| Hold notes | Keep the key or pad pressed | Keep the pad pressed |

## Features

- **Tap and hold notes.** Holds must stay pressed until the body finishes crossing the line.
- **Adaptive fall speed.** Travel time scales with each track's BPM, so slower songs stay readable and faster songs stay reaction-heavy.
- **Automatic charting.** Built-in tracks are composed procedurally; imported audio is analyzed locally with Web Audio/FFT onset detection and autocorrelation tempo estimation.
- **Local-only imports.** Audio is decoded and charted in the browser. The file is never uploaded, and imported tracks live for the current session.
- **Persistent best scores.** Best score and accuracy per track/difficulty are stored in `localStorage`.
- **Desktop and mobile.** Four touch pads, safe-area-aware layout, responsive HUD, pause, retry, and results screens.

## Difficulties

| Difficulty | Note size | Fall time* | Max simultaneous | Density |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Normal | Large | 2.46 s | 1 note | Relaxed |
| Hard | Medium | 1.91 s | 2 notes | Syncopated |
| Extreme | Small | 1.43 s | 3 notes | Constant chords |
| Demon | Tiny | 1.06 s | 4 notes | Maximum pressure |

\*For the 112 BPM built-in track. Charts also adapt to each song's tempo.

## Project Structure

- `index.html` — app shell, menu, game screen, overlays.
- `css/style.css` — layout, theme, responsive and safe-area rules.
- `js/data.js` — difficulties, built-in track metadata, helpers.
- `js/composition.js` — procedural composition and fallback synthesis.
- `js/chart.js` — chart generation for taps, holds, chords, and travel time.
- `js/audio-engine.js` — AudioContext, decoding, onset/tempo analysis, hit SFX.
- `js/game.js` — canvas renderer, loop, input, scoring, pause, results.
- `js/app.js` — UI state, track/difficulty selection, import flow, best scores.
- `assets/audio/` — pre-rendered built-in tracks.
- `assets/fonts/` — local Sora and Space Mono subsets.

## Assumptions

- Modern browser with Web Audio, ES modules, and Canvas 2D support.
- Imported tracks are intentionally session-only (no persistent IndexedDB storage).
- Charts are generated deterministically from each track's seed or detected events, so replaying the same track and difficulty produces the same chart.
